## Predictors: Socio-demographic characteristics of residents
- Some input data comes linked to the original parcel dataset, where the parcels are not merged. Thus, the variables must be assigned via the original data set. Therefore, we use the linking dataset to aggregate the information to the merged parcels. 
- In the end of the script we join all predictor variables calculated so far together. 

## Input data
- Pre-processed parcel dataset of 2023
- Basic parcel dataset 2023
- Linking dataset basic parcels - merged parcels

Additional input
- Information on housholds/inhabitants 2020 and 2023

Results from prior steps which are all joined here:
- Pre-processed parcel dataset with geometric and location information
- Pre-processed parcel dataset with largest non-built-up area

```{r, include=FALSE}
## Parcel datasets
parcels_raw <- st_read("./data_prep_output_2023/parcels_04_final_data_2023.gpkg")
zuordnung_23_21 <- read_rds("./data_prep_output_2023/link_parcels_03_merged_2023_2021.rds")
parcels_base_raw <- st_read("./data_prep_output_2023/parcels_01_base_2023.gpkg")

## Input new variables
par_inhabitants_2020 <- read.csv("./data_input/Bevölkerung/Bevölkerung/FLURSTUECKE23_EWO20.csv", sep=";")
par_inhabitants_2023 <- read.csv("./data_input/Bevölkerung/Bevölkerung/FLURSTUECKE23_EWO23.csv", sep=";")

## Results from earlier calculation steps
parcels_geom <- read_sf("./data_prep_output_2023/parcels_predictors_01_2023.gpkg")
parcels_largest_nbu <- read_sf("./data_prep_output_2023/parcels_predictors_02_2023.gpkg") %>% 
  st_drop_geometry()
```

## Prepare and join inhabitants
- The inhabitant data set is created for the original plots. Therefore, the figures for merged plots must be aggregated.
- As we inserted buildings of 2021 in the 2023 dataset, for these parcels we need to include information on inhabitant from the respective year. 
- The age of the inhabitants is provided in age groups. 
- ave_age_par: To calculate the average age per parcel, we use the mean age in each group (e.g. 10-15 = 12.5). 
- persons_total_par: To calculate the total number of persons per parcel, we sum up the number of persons in all age groups.
- only_75_older_par: Is a TRUE/FALSE variable which is TRUE if there are only persons of the 75 and older present.
- under_16_present_par: TRUE if there is a person under 16 present. 

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Add a "Year" column
par_inhabitants_2020$Jahr <- 2020
par_inhabitants_2023$Jahr <- 2023

# Combine both tables
par_inhabitants <- rbind(par_inhabitants_2020, par_inhabitants_2023)

par_inhabitants_joined <- zuordnung_23_21 %>%
  left_join(par_inhabitants %>% mutate(id_par = FLSTNR) %>% select(-FLSTNR))

par_inhabitants_joined$Join_Count <- NULL

par_inhabitants_sum <- par_inhabitants_joined %>%
  group_by(id_par_merge, Jahr) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  filter(EN14 != 0)

par_inhabitants_sum <- par_inhabitants_sum %>%
  arrange(id_par_merge, desc(Jahr)) %>%  # Priorisiere 2023
  group_by(id_par_merge) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

# Von breit nach lang: EN1 bis EN14 werden in zwei Spalten umgewandelt: "age_classes_code" und "persons"
par_inhabitants_sum_long <- pivot_longer(
  par_inhabitants_sum,
  cols = starts_with("EN"),
  names_to = "age_classes_code",
  values_to = "persons"
)

# Rename age classes and add age_mean
age_classes_labels <- c(
  EN1 = "0 to 2", EN2 = "3 to 5", EN3 = "6 to 9", EN4 = "10 to 15", EN5 = "16 to 18",
  EN6 = "19 to 20", EN7 = "21 to 24", EN8 = "25 to 29", EN9 = "30 to 44", EN10 = "45 to 59",
  EN11 = "60 to 64", EN12 = "65 to 74", EN13 = "75 and older", EN14 = "total"
)

par_inhabitants_sum_long <- par_inhabitants_sum_long %>%
  mutate(age_classes = age_classes_labels[age_classes_code]) %>%
  mutate(age_mean = case_when(
    age_classes == "0 to 2" ~ 1,
    age_classes == "3 to 5" ~ 4,
    age_classes == "6 to 9" ~ 7.5,
    age_classes == "10 to 15" ~ 12.5,
    age_classes == "16 to 18" ~ 17,
    age_classes == "19 to 20" ~ 19.5,
    age_classes == "21 to 24" ~ 22.5,
    age_classes == "25 to 29" ~ 27,
    age_classes == "30 to 44" ~ 37,
    age_classes == "45 to 59" ~ 52,
    age_classes == "60 to 64" ~ 62,
    age_classes == "65 to 74" ~ 69.5,
    age_classes == "75 and older" ~ 80,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )) %>%
  # Remove the "total" row, as it interferes with mean calculations and dummy variables
  filter(age_classes != "total")

# Calculate average age (16+), dummy variables, and total number of persons per parcel

par_inhabitants_summary_extended <- par_inhabitants_sum_long %>%
  group_by(id_par_merge) %>%
  summarise(
    # Calculate the sum of persons for relevant age groups
    persons_16_plus = sum(persons[age_classes %in% c("16 to 18", "19 to 20", "21 to 24", "25 to 29", "30 to 44", "45 to 59", "60 to 64", "65 to 74", "75 and older")], na.rm = TRUE),
    persons_75_older = sum(persons[age_classes == "75 and older"], na.rm = TRUE),
    persons_under_16 = sum(persons[age_classes %in% c("0 to 2", "3 to 5", "6 to 9", "10 to 15")], na.rm = TRUE),
    persons_total_calc = sum(persons, na.rm = TRUE), # Total number of persons from all age classes (excluding "total" row)

    # Calculate the weighted age for the 16+ group
    weighted_age_16_plus = sum(persons[age_classes %in% c("16 to 18", "19 to 20", "21 to 24", "25 to 29", "30 to 44", "45 to 59", "60 to 64", "65 to 74", "75 and older")] *
                                 age_mean[age_classes %in% c("16 to 18", "19 to 20", "21 to 24", "25 to 29", "30 to 44", "45 to 59", "60 to 64", "65 to 74", "75 and older")], na.rm = TRUE),

    # Average age of the 16+ group (NA if no persons 16+ present)
    ave_age_par = if_else(persons_16_plus > 0, weighted_age_16_plus / persons_16_plus, NA_real_),

    # Dummy variable: parcel contains ONLY persons 75 and older
    only_75_older_par = if_else(persons_75_older > 0 & persons_75_older == persons_total_calc, 1, 0),

    # Dummy variable: parcel contains children/teenagers under 16
    under_16_present_par = if_else(persons_under_16 > 0, 1, 0)
  ) %>%
  # Select the desired columns, including the total number of persons
  select(id_par_merge,
         persons_total_par = persons_total_calc, # Here the variable is added and renamed
         ave_age_par,
         only_75_older_par,
         under_16_present_par) %>% 
  mutate(exclude_age = if_else(is.na(ave_age_par), "exclude", NA))
```

### Final dataset inhabitants
- Contains some NA for ave_age_par if only persons under 16 are present -> We created a column with exclude_age which can be use late to filter these cases. 
- By joining the data back to the whole dataset, we have more NA as the input dataset contains only parcels with inhabitant. Thus, for all other parcels we set the NA to 0. 

```{r, include=FALSE}
par_inhabitants_fin <- parcels_raw %>% 
  left_join(par_inhabitants_summary_extended, by = c("id_par_merge")) %>% 
  mutate(persons_total_par = if_else(is.na(persons_total_par), 0, persons_total_par),
         ave_age_par = if_else(is.na(ave_age_par), 0, ave_age_par),
         only_75_older_par = if_else(is.na(only_75_older_par), 0, only_75_older_par),
         under_16_present_par = if_else(is.na(under_16_present_par), 0, under_16_present_par))
```

## Combine all datasets
```{r, include=FALSE}
parcels_fin <- par_inhabitants_fin %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  left_join(parcels_largest_nbu) %>% 
  left_join(parcels_geom)

summary(parcels_fin)
```

## Output
```{r, include=FALSE}
st_write(parcels_fin, "./data_prep_output_2023/parcels_predictors_03_2023.gpkg", delete_layer = TRUE)
```

